step_by_step_browser_trace.result: App shell rendered normally; login screen was bypassed successfully; no console errors observed.

step_by_step_browser_trace.result: Served live page is the main W4 UI, not the older ux-ui-prototype upload flow. Real controls present: #uploadCompanySelect, #uploadFileInput, #uploadSubmitBtn.

step_by_step_browser_trace.result: UI action fired, but backend returned 500 on approve-all. Documents stayed in review_scan and Review Mapping remained empty.

step_by_step_browser_trace.action: Select one document and click single Approve
step_by_step_browser_trace.result: Single-document approve also returned 500. This confirms the first reproducible failing point after Processing is not upload UI wiring but the approve endpoints themselves.

upload_phase.diagnosis: The live Upload UI does not auto-upload on file selection. It waits for the explicit upload click, then fires the correct company-scoped POST endpoint.

upload_and_processing_trace.conclusion: No browser console error or client-side JS exception blocked the upload or processing path during the successful trace.

console_errors: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 ()
login_form_probe_note.conclusion: This came from invalid app-login credential attempts during setup only, not from the token-authenticated browser flow used for the actual diagnosis.

diagnosis_conclusion.summary: The routine browser flow on the live served W4 page is workable through Upload and Processing when executed on the correct screen with a selected company and an explicit upload click. The originally suspected 'UI never sends POST /documents/upload' condition is not reproducible on this path.
what_was_proven: Pending files exist in UI state before clicking upload.
No upload POST is expected before the explicit upload click on the current live UI.
The click sends the correct company-scoped POST /api/v1/companies/{id}/documents/upload request and receives 200.
Processing sends real POST /api/v1/documents/{id}/process calls and receives 200.
Review Scan displays the newly processed documents afterward.

first_reproducible_failing_point.effect: Documents remain in review_scan and never advance into Review Mapping.

diagnosis_conclusion.interpretation: This is no longer a primary FRONTEND UX / WIRING issue for Upload -> Processing. The next narrow defect is a BACKEND CONTRACT/runtime failure on approve endpoints, with a secondary documentation/usage note that the live UI requires an explicit upload click and does not auto-upload on file selection.

recommended_next_owner.reason: Reproducible backend/API failure after processing succeeds; not a browser-only issue.
Same backend defect family as approve-all; blocks Review Mapping transition.
Current live Upload screen requires explicit company selection and explicit upload click; lack of POST before click is expected behavior, not itself a bug.
